requirement_text:
Functional Requirements

2.2.1 Enable agents to broadcast a message to all the agents within the same local network.
2.2.2 Enable agents to multicast a message to all the agents within the same multicast address.
2.2.3 Enable agents to unicast a message to other agents within organization. 
2.2.4 Allow agents to choose among unicast, multicast and broadcast communication.
2.2.5 Allow agents to join and leave multicast group.
2.2.6 Provide message encryption and decryption techniques for secured communication.
2.2.7 Allow agents to choose to encrypt or not to encrypt message

Use case Scenarios

Use Case 1: Notify join/leave multicast group
1. Message is encrypted or Message is not encrypted.
2. An agent sends notify to join/leave multicast group.
3. Message is decrypted only if Message is encrypted.
For example, Agent_B and Agent_D belong to the same group, and then Agent_B
wants to leave the group and Agent_A wants to join the group. In this situation, when reorganization occurs, Agent_A who is previously not part of the group may send notify message to join the group, and Agent_B who is previously part of the group, may send notify message to leave the group. For instance, Agent_B suffers a failure in one of its
 
capabilities and does not want to receive any further message from the group. Agent_A who may have capability to substitute Agent_B is needed to be part of the group. This involves sending notify of join and leave the group.

Use Case 2: Send/Receive Unicast
1. Message is encrypted or Message is not encrypted.
2. An agent sends unicast message to another agent.
3. Another agent receives message.
4. Message is decrypted only if Message is encrypted.
In this situation, Agent_A wants to communicate with Agent_B. This direct communication can happen between any two agents within organization.

Use Case 3: Send/Receive Multicast
1. Message is encrypted or Message is not encrypted.
2. An agent sends multicast message to the group (multicast address).
3. Other agents in the group receive message.
4. Message is decrypted only if Message is encrypted
In this situation, Agent_A wants to send a message to everyone within the group,
assuming that Agent_A, Agent_B and Agent_C subscribe to the same multicast address. This involves the multicast communication since other agents who do not belong to the group cannot receive this message. For instance, an agent may want to inform everyone in the group when the assigned tasks are completed. This is more effective than in unicast communication since only one copy is sent. Also, using bidding/market-based protocols fit well with this kind of communication. An agent may request a bid from other agents
for doing some tasks.

Use Case 4: Send/Receive Broadcast
1. An agent sends message to everyone in the same local network
2. Other agent in the same local network receive message
In this situation, Agent_A wants to send a message to everyone within the same local
network that agent A belongs to. This involves the broadcast communication since any agent in the same local network as Agent_A can receive this message. For instance, when a new agent who does not previously exist in that local network wants to announce the existence to other agents.

review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers the main required communication modes, encryption choice, multicast join/leave notification, and delivery paths. However, it conflates independent choices in a way that prevents some required combinations from being modeled correctly, and it omits an explicit no-encryption path after the encryption decision.

defects.description: The diagram routes all three communication modes through the multicast-group-operation decision node, which makes join/leave notification part of every unicast and broadcast path instead of only the multicast-group use case.
defects.evidence: Requirement R5/R6/R11 require join/leave multicast group notification, while R3/R13, R1/R17, and R2/R15 define separate unicast, broadcast, and multicast behaviors. In the diagram, N5 fans out to N6/N7 as well as N8/N9/N10, so a selected unicast or broadcast path still passes through the multicast join/leave choice.
defects.suggested_action: Separate multicast-group join/leave handling from the unicast/broadcast communication branches. Keep join/leave notifications only on the multicast-group management path, and let unicast and broadcast proceed directly to their send/delivery flows.

defects.description: The encryption choice is not modeled as an explicit alternative flow for the 'not encrypted' case after the decision. Instead, the unencrypted path is merged into the later communication-mode decision without a corresponding no-encryption action or explicit bypass of encryption/decryption.
defects.evidence: R9 requires agents to choose whether to encrypt a message, R10 says encryption occurs only if chosen, and R12 says decryption occurs only if the message is encrypted. The diagram has N3 -> N4 for encryption, but the not-encrypted branch E7 goes straight to N5 and later to N11, with no explicit no-encryption continuation that preserves the intended alternative flow for the message.
defects.suggested_action: Model the not-encrypted branch explicitly as a direct continuation from the encryption decision to the downstream communication path, and ensure decryption is reachable only from the encrypted branch.

strengths: All required communication modes are represented: unicast, multicast, and broadcast.
Encryption and decryption actions are present, and decryption is guarded by the encrypted condition.
Join and leave multicast group notifications are both modeled.
Receive actions for unicast, multicast, and broadcast are included.
unsupported_behaviors: The current control flow implies join/leave multicast-group notification is part of unicast and broadcast communication paths, which is not supported by the requirements.

review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers the main communication modes, encryption choice, multicast join/leave notifications, and delivery actions, but it has one semantic/control-flow issue: the multicast path does not correctly terminate in the receive-and-finish sequence when encryption is selected, and the broadcast branch is modeled inconsistently from the other branches. Overall coverage is mostly good, but execution paths are not fully coherent.

defects.description: The encrypted multicast path does not correctly model delivery to recipients after decryption. From the encryption decision, the encrypted multicast branch goes N11 -> N12 -> N14, but the diagram also routes N12 -> N13 and does not provide a distinct, required multicast delivery continuation that clearly represents other agents in the group receiving the decrypted multicast message. This creates ambiguous or incorrect control flow for the encrypted multicast scenario.
defects.evidence: Requirements R15 and R16 require that an agent sends a multicast message to the group and other agents in the group receive it, with R12 requiring decryption only if the message is encrypted. The diagram sends encrypted messages from N11 to N12, then from N12 both to N13 and N14, making unicast receipt reachable from a multicast/decryption path and failing to clearly preserve the multicast-specific receive flow.
defects.suggested_action: Separate the encrypted multicast delivery path from the unicast delivery path. After N12, route only to a multicast-receive action for group recipients, and ensure unicast receive is reachable only from the unicast branch.

defects.description: The broadcast branch bypasses the encryption decision in a way that makes the broadcast flow inconsistent with the rest of the modeled communication modes. N10 goes directly to N15 and only later the diagram reaches termination, while the encryption decision N11 is only evaluated for the other branches. As a result, broadcast delivery is modeled as incompatible with the encrypted/not-encrypted choice even though the requirements state that messages may be encrypted or not encrypted for communication scenarios generally.
defects.evidence: The use case scenarios state for communication that a message is encrypted or not encrypted, and R9 allows agents to choose whether to encrypt a message. In the diagram, the broadcast path N10 -> N15 is detached from N11, unlike unicast and multicast, which both flow through encryption/decryption. This makes the broadcast execution path semantically inconsistent with the shared encryption choice.
defects.suggested_action: If broadcast messages are also subject to the encryption choice, route the broadcast branch through the encryption decision and decryption check as appropriate. If broadcast is intentionally excluded from encryption, make that exclusion explicit in the model and requirements mapping.

review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers the core communication modes, encryption choice, multicast join/leave notification, and delivery paths. However, there are semantic control-flow issues that make the communication-mode selection and delivery logic inconsistent with the requirements, especially for broadcast and the encryption/decryption flow.

defects.description: The communication-mode decision is not modeled as a proper three-way choice: the broadcast and unicast branches both route back into the encryption decision node instead of leading directly into their respective send actions from the communication-mode decision.
defects.evidence: R4 requires agents to choose among unicast, multicast, and broadcast communication. In the diagram, N2 has a multicast branch to N5, but unicast and broadcast branches (E4, E5) go to N3, and later multicast/broadcast send actions are only reached via N5. This makes the choice structure semantically inconsistent with a direct three-option communication selection.
defects.suggested_action: Rewire the communication-mode decision so each of the three choices leads to the corresponding communication path: unicast to unicast send, multicast to multicast group handling/send, and broadcast to broadcast send, without incorrectly routing unicast and broadcast through the encryption choice unless that is explicitly intended as a separate shared step.

defects.description: The broadcast path is incorrectly forced through the encryption/decryption handling, although the broadcast use case and requirements do not require encryption or decryption as part of broadcast delivery.
defects.evidence: R17 and R18 specify only that an agent sends a broadcast message to everyone in the same local network and that other agents receive it. Unlike the multicast and unicast scenarios, the broadcast requirements do not include encryption/decryption. Yet E18 sends the broadcast path into N11, where encryption is optionally handled and then broadcast delivery proceeds via E22 or would be decrypted via N12 in the encrypted case.
defects.suggested_action: Remove broadcast from the encryption decision flow. Route broadcast directly from the broadcast send action to broadcast receipt/delivery, and keep encryption/decryption only on the communication paths that are required to support it.

defects.description: The encrypted multicast/unicast flow does not terminate correctly after decryption, because decryption is followed by delivery nodes that then terminate, but the control structure also allows the unencrypted branch to terminate directly; this creates an inconsistent delivery model where decryption is treated as a shared post-processing step rather than part of a valid encrypted receive path for all affected communication modes.
defects.evidence: R12 requires decryption only if the message is encrypted. For encrypted unicast/multicast, the diagram routes N11 -> N12 and then N12 -> N13/N14. However, the same decision node N11 also directly routes unencrypted traffic to N13/N14. The resulting structure conflates receive/deliver with decryption in a way that is not clearly consistent across all message types, especially since delivery is modeled after decryption rather than as part of the receive action itself.
defects.suggested_action: Model encrypted and unencrypted receive paths more explicitly: after the encrypted branch, decrypt and then deliver to the corresponding receive action; after the unencrypted branch, go directly to the corresponding receive action. Ensure the termination semantics are identical for both paths and clearly tied to each communication mode.

review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers the main communication modes, encryption choice, and multicast join/leave notification flows, but it has a significant semantic issue in the encrypted receive paths: decrypted messages are delivered only to multicast and unicast recipients, while the broadcast path bypasses the encryption/decryption decision entirely. This creates an inconsistent and partially unsupported interaction between encryption and delivery compared with the requirements and use cases.

defects.description: The broadcast path does not participate in the encryption/decryption decision, so an encrypted broadcast message cannot be decrypted before delivery, and the diagram implies broadcast delivery is always direct regardless of the encryption choice.
defects.evidence: Requirements R9, R10, and R12 require agents to choose whether to encrypt a message and to decrypt it only if it is encrypted.
